question: What is the default failsafe action on the DJI Matrice 30T if the aircraft and controller disconnect?

intake.focus: default failsafe action after loss of control link
intake.reason: Request guidance from manuals on lost link behavior and failsafe action

brief.short_answer: FAA guidance describes starting emergency or contingency procedures for loss of control link and attempting to reestablish the control link if possible, with guidance to land, hover, or use a return-to-home sequence if VLOS cannot be regained. The DJI Matrice 30T manual states RTH can be triggered actively by the user, on low battery, or when the control signal is lost, and that the aircraft will automatically land at the Home Point if conditions are normal. The incident reports (unverified) describe lost-link events with RTH on back-to-back hops, RTH at programmed altitude without issue, and RTH initiation without response.

claims.text: FAA AC 107-2A states: If connection cannot be reestablished, start emergency or contingency procedures for loss of control link. This triggers loss of control link and requires initiating emergency procedures when the link is not reestablished.
claims.quote: If connection cannot be reestablished, start emergency or contingency procedures for loss of control link.

claims.text: FAA AC 107-2A states: Describe what will be done if the hazard occurs. Example: Try to reestablish control link connection with the small unmanned aircraft. This compels attempting to reestablish the control link when the hazard occurs.
claims.quote: Describe what will be done if the hazard occurs. Example: Try to reestablish control link connection with the small unmanned aircraft.

claims.text: FAA AC 107-2A states: If the remote PIC cannot regain VLOS, the remote PIC or person manipulating the controls should follow pre-determined procedures for the loss of VLOS.
claims.quote: If the remote PIC cannot regain VLOS, the remote PIC or person manipulating the controls should follow pre-determined procedures for the loss of VLOS.

claims.text: FAA AC 107-2A states: The remote PIC may need to land the small unmanned aircraft immediately, enter hover mode, or employ a return-to-home sequence.
claims.quote: the remote PIC may need to land the small unmanned aircraft immediately, enter hover mode, or employ a return-to-home sequence
conditions: loss of control or VLOS considerations

claims.text: RTH can be triggered in three ways: the user actively triggers, the aircraft has low battery, or the control signal between the remote controller and the aircraft is lost (Home Point recorded; positioning system functioning normally).
claims.quote: RTH can be triggered in three ways: the user actively triggers, the aircraft has low battery, or the control signal between the remote controller and the aircraft is lost

claims.text: If the Home Point is recorded and positioning is normal, when the RTH is triggered the aircraft will automatically fly back and land at the Home Point.
claims.quote: the aircraft will automatically fly back and land at the Home Point

claims.quote: Lost link and RTH occurred twice on back-to-back hops

claims.text: The reporter states: "UAS RTH at programmed altitude without issue."
claims.quote: UAS RTH at programmed altitude without issue

claims.text: The reporter states: "RTH initiated but did not respond."
claims.quote: RTH initiated but did not respond

gaps.text: FAA: if link cannot be reestablished, start emergency procedures. DJI: RTH can be automatically triggered when control signal is lost.
FAA: attempt to reestablish control link; DJI: RTH triggered when link lost—two different prescribed responses.
The passage addresses loss of visual line of sight, not loss of link or hazard scenarios; no support for the claimed condition.
No verified evidence that RTH is the sole/default response to loss of control link across sources.
